text.p: Here are highlights from Polish newspapers this morning.
FRONT PAGE POLITICAL NEWS.
RZECZPOSPOLITA

- Around 29 percent of Poles express support for the ex-communist Democratic Left Alliance (SLD), 27 percent for the rightwing Solidarity Electoral Action (AWS), 14 percent are ready to vote for the centrist Union for Freedom (UW) and 9 percent support the Polish Peasant Party (PSL), an April survey by the PBS polling institute said.
- Parliamentary committees have drafted a bill calling for civil servants to limit outside business interests.
ECONOMIC AND MARKET NEWS
RZECZPOSPOLITA
- Poland is planning to set up Polski Wegiel SA, a coal mining industry administration body with powers similar to the former mining ministry, a cabinet working document said.
- ABB
Poland made a net profit of 115 million zlotys last year, showing an 85.5 percent growth compared with results in 1995 when it earned 62 million zlotys, the company said.
- The U.S. Eximbank has underwritten a contract to purchase new Boeing aircraft by Poland's national flag carrier PLL LOT, the airline's president Jan Litwinski said.
- Kredyt Bank (KB) in Warsaw will launch a 10 million M-series share issue priced at 8.3 zlotys per share on Monday, KB said.

- Poland will invest 85 million zlotys in construction of an energy transmission line to link Poland's Krosno and Slovakia's Lemeszany and 27.6 million zlotys in development of the Krosno power plant in southeastern Poland.

- Poland's finance ministry is not planning to cut the 22 percent VAT rate on oranges, grapefruits and lemons, the ministry said. The EU has sought the cut as fruits imported from Poland carry a seven percent rate while Poland's imports of Spanish oranges are burdened with a 22 percent VAT.

- Farmers supplying sugar beets to the Cukrownia Ropczyce sugar plant formed a mutual insurance trust to insure crops against hail and flood. When not fully paid out in damages, the premiums will be refunded to policy holders, the new fund said.
DZIENNIK PRAWA I GOSPODARKI
- ABB Poland is planning to buy the ZWAR high voltage measuring equiment maker in Warsaw to be privatised in the next three to four months, ABB Poland president Miroslaw Gryszka said.

- The board of the Bank Rozwoju Exportu (BRE) export development bank will recommend increasing the bank's share capital to 74 million zlotys from the present 68 million zlotys at BRE's general shareholders' meeting on May 28. The new issue of up to 4.5 million shares will be offered to Commerzbank, as BRE hopes to gain access to Commerzbank's advanced banking technologies, BRE's board said.
GAZETA WYBORCZA
- The Brok brewery in Koszalin, northern Poland, will sell 287,500 C-series shares priced at 24 zlotys per share in a public offer on the parallel or over-the-counter market in May this year.
ZYCIE
- Around 500 pharmaceutical firms from 30 countries are exhibiting at the Eleventh International Pharmacutical Fair in Warsaw this week. Polish companies make up 40 percent of exhibitors.
PARKIET
- Investment in the Celuloza Swiecie paper plant will bring moderate profits in 1997 but growth perspectives in 1998 appear excellent, a recent report by the IB Austria Securities said.
-- Warsaw Newsroom +48 22 653 9700
